# Outline: which k benchmarks to run, and how well do they predict the rest?

(Outline revision 1. Built from the `Brief` of idea-repo, revision 3 (2026-11-25 16:08 UTC). It says what to test, not what a result must be. Thresholds, definitions and hypotheses H1-H4 are the Brief's and are not restated in full; where this page names one, the Brief governs.)

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Evaluating a new model on N benchmarks is costly; leaderboards hold a history matrix of M models x N benchmarks. An evaluator can run only k benchmarks and wants the other N-k scores. Prior work shrinks the items *inside* one benchmark, or shows that benchmark scores are low-dimensional, but does not treat "which k to run" as a design problem, give a k-versus-error law, or test the answer where it matters: for a new family or a newer, stronger model. We (i) set up a leakage-free, family-clustered, paired protocol for this question; (ii) give a closed-form k-curve for a linear-Gaussian latent-factor model and check it in three tiers; (iii) compare greedy Bayesian A-optimal selection with random and standard selectors under a fixed predictor grid; and (iv) report honestly how much of the answer survives family/time shift and in which data regimes. The method is a known toolkit (PPCA/EM + Gaussian conditioning + greedy A-optimal); the contribution is the protocol, the finding, and the verified theory, in that order.

**Headline claim (to be set by results; wording fixed only after H2/H3).** The paper is built around the primary result: error and closure C(k) as a function of k on real matrices, under family-held-out evaluation. The selector is *not* the headline unless it beats random under shift by the Brief's margin. Three headline forms are all acceptable, and the data choose: (A) "informed selection beats random clearly"; (B) "random is nearly as good, and coherence explains why"; (C) "a dominant general factor means k = 1-2 gives most of it, the rest is slow".

"""Table 2 (claim C1): k* per data set, closure level and predictor, with family-bootstrap CI and censoring.

k* = smallest k whose closure to the leave-one-benchmark-out reference reaches the level (grouped K-fold, greedy A).
A k* beyond the grid is printed as ">G" (G = largest k tried), never dropped; a CI end of G+1 is printed as ">G".
Headline = the smaller of the two predictors' k* (experiment-repo's definition); H1 outcome is judged on it at level 0.9.
"""
import argparse, os, json
import pandas as pd
import style

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--results", required=True); p.add_argument("--out", default="out")
p.add_argument("--split", default="grouped"); p.add_argument("--selector", default="greedyA")
a = p.parse_args()
ks = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(a.results, "kstar.csv"))
h1 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(a.results, "h1.csv"))
gp = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(a.results, "gap.csv"))
ks = ks[(ks.split == a.split) & (ks.selector == a.selector) & (ks.reference == "lobo")]
h1 = h1[(h1.split == a.split) & (h1.selector == a.selector)].set_index("dataset")
gp = gp[(gp.split == a.split) & (gp.design == "fixed") & (gp.comparison == "primary") & (gp.k.astype(str) == "grid_avg")].set_index("dataset")
DS = ["mteb_eng", "mteb_multi", "helm_mmlu"]; LEV = [0.8, 0.9, 0.95]


def cell(r):
    g = int(r.grid_max)
    lo = f"{int(round(r.kstar_ci_lo))}" if r.kstar_ci_lo <= g else f">{g}"
    hi = f"{int(round(r.kstar_ci_hi))}" if r.kstar_ci_hi <= g else f">{g}"
    k = f">{g}" if r.censored else f"{int(round(r.kstar))}"
    return f"{k} [{lo}, {hi}]"


H1 = {"dominated by general factor": "dominated by one factor", "above window": "above window", "knee near r_eff": "knee near $r_{\\rm eff}$"}
lines = [r"\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccrc@{}}", r"\toprule",
         r"Data ($r_{\rm eff}$) & Level & PPCA & Best simple & Headline (min) & Cens.\ \% & $\pm$ H2 gap \\", r"\midrule"]
for i, ds in enumerate(DS):
    d = ks[ks.dataset == ds]
    for lv in LEV:
        row = lambda pr: d[(d.predictor == pr) & (d.level == lv)].iloc[0]
        f, b, h = row("fa"), row("best_simple"), row("headline")
        first = f"{style.DATASET_SHORT[ds]} ({int(h.r_eff)})" if lv == LEV[0] else ""
        last = f"{gp.loc[ds].ci_halfwidth:.3f}" if lv == LEV[0] else ""
        lines.append(f"{first} & {lv:.2f} & {cell(f)} & {cell(b)} & {cell(h)} & {100 * h.share_censored_boot:.0f} & {last} " + r"\\")
    lines.append(r"\addlinespace" if i < len(DS) - 1 else "")
lines += [r"\bottomrule", r"\end{tabular}"]
out = "\n".join(l for l in lines if l != "")
CAP = (r"$k^*$ for closure to the leave-one-benchmark-out reference at three levels, with the family-clustered bootstrap CI in brackets (grouped $K$-fold, greedy A). "
       r"``$>G$'' means the level is not reached within the largest $k$ tried, $G$. Headline: the smaller of the PPCA and best-simple $k^*$; "
       r"Cens.\ \% is the share of bootstrap replicates of the headline $k^*$ beyond the grid. "
       r"H1 outcome at level 0.90 (headline): " + "; ".join(f"{style.DATASET_SHORT[ds]} {H1[h1.loc[ds].h1_outcome]}" for ds in DS) +
       r". Last column: half-width of the family-bootstrap CI of the grid-averaged greedy-minus-random gap (Fig.~\ref{fig:gap}), in standardised RMSE.")
tex = "% generated by figtab-repo figs/table2_kstar.py from results/kstar.csv, h1.csv, gap.csv; do not edit\n" + \
      "\\begin{table}[t]\n\\caption{" + CAP + "}\n\\label{tab:kstar}\n\\centering\\footnotesize\n" + out + "\n\\end{table}\n"
os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(a.out, "table2_kstar.tex"), "w").write(tex)
json.dump(dict(table="table2_kstar", split=a.split, selector=a.selector, reference="lobo", design="fixed",
               inputs={f: style.sha(os.path.join(a.results, f)) for f in ("kstar.csv", "h1.csv", "gap.csv")}),
          open(os.path.join(a.out, "table2_kstar.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print(tex)

def save(fig, name, outdir, sidecar):
    """Write <name>.pdf and <name>.json (what the figure was computed on)."""
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    pdf = os.path.join(outdir, name + ".pdf")
    fig.savefig(pdf)
    sidecar = dict(sidecar, figure=name, generated=datetime.date.today().isoformat(),
                   width_in=fig.get_size_inches()[0], height_in=fig.get_size_inches()[1])
    with open(os.path.join(outdir, name + ".json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(sidecar, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    plt.close(fig)
    return pdf

# Results and the conditions they hold under (experiment-repo, as of commit after 077ae91)

Every number below is read from a file in `results/` (file named in brackets). Primary design: grouped 10-fold by model family (21 / 247-column MTEB multi / 79 HELM
models), fixed 30 % target columns, greedy A-optimal selector, FA predictor unless said otherwise; intervals are family-clustered bootstrap (B=2000, seed 0).
Metrics are RMSE on the original standardised scale. Transform (identity or logit) was chosen on training folds by held-out likelihood:
helm_mmlu logit, mteb_eng identity, mteb_multi logit [`transform.csv`]. Departures from the Brief are in `DEVIATIONS.md`.

## H2: greedy A vs random, grid average over k=1..min(10,N/2) [`gap.csv`, `robustness.csv`]
* Gap in RMSE (greedy A minus random), CI: helm_mmlu -0.044 [-0.065, -0.026] (-7.6 % of random); mteb_eng -0.038 [-0.058, -0.013] (-6.1 %);
  mteb_multi -0.076 [-0.085, -0.066] (-11.3 %). The CI excludes 0 on all three; the pre-registered margin (gap >= 10 % of random RMSE) is met only on mteb_multi.
* Same sign on random and time-forward splits (gap.csv, exploratory rows). Under the non-chosen transform on mteb_eng (logit) the gap shrinks to -2.6 %
  [`robustness.csv`]; so the result depends on the transform choice there.
* Adaptive (per-model, local-A) selection in the identity space [`adaptive.csv`]: against greedy A the RMSE gain is nil on mteb_eng (FA +0.0003, CI [-0.010, 0.016]),
  helm_mmlu (FA -0.005, CI [-0.010, 0.003]) and small on mteb_multi (FA -0.014 [-0.030, -0.005]; kNN -0.008 [-0.014, -0.003]). Greedy A is within about
  0.01 RMSE of the adaptive rule everywhere.

## H1 and k* [`h1.csv`, `kstar.csv`, `closure.csv`]
* Headline k* (90 % closure to the leave-one-benchmark-out reference, grouped): helm_mmlu 1 (CI 1-2, "dominated by general factor"); mteb_eng 9 (CI 3-31, "above window");
  mteb_multi 30 = grid maximum (CI 8-31, "above window"). Time-forward split: mteb_eng 30 (31.6 % of bootstrap draws censored), mteb_multi 15.
* k* is fragile on the two MTEB matrices: intervals are wide, depend on the threshold, the predictor (mteb_eng FA-only 20 vs headline 9) and, on mteb_multi,
  on the transform (identity gives 15, logit is censored beyond the grid for FA). Report k* with its CI and censoring share, never as a point value.
* Per-benchmark skill at k=3 and 10 [`per_benchmark_skill.csv`]: median skill of FA with greedy A is 0.83 / 0.84 (helm_mmlu), 0.73 / 0.83 (mteb_eng), 0.75 / 0.80 (mteb_multi);
  the lower tail is heavy on MTEB (16-17 % of benchmarks below 0.5 at k=10; a few benchmarks below 0, i.e. worse than the column mean).

## H4 theory check (Risk formula against measured held-out error) [`theory_gap.csv`, `theory_shape.csv`, `coherence.csv`]
* Median relative gap on the reducible part: synthetic true model 0.5 %; synthetic fitted 20 % (M=60 columns: 27 %) falling to 6.5 % at M=250 and 1.5 % at M=2000;
  parametric bootstrap from the fitted real models 16-24 %; real data 36 % (mteb_multi), 47 % (mteb_eng), 69 % (helm_mmlu). H4 (<= 15 % real, <= 10 % synthetic fitted)
  therefore **fails on real data** and on fitted synthetic data at small M; it holds at M >= 250 synthetic.
* The gap is mostly a roughly constant offset (about 0.08 in squared standardised units at k_max on the real tier): the k-dependent part is predicted much better (median relative

shown.message:
The figures and tables are delivered to `paper-repo` `dev` (commit c0b2724), all built from `experiment-repo` results at commit 61f6ba3. I did not build the full paper PDF, so nothing is placed in the text yet. The report role places them using the labels in `paper-repo`#4.

- **Figures:** Figs. 1–5 and 7, and appendix Figs. A1–A3.
- **Tables:** Tables 1–4, and appendix Tables A1–A5.
- **Alongside each:** a JSON sidecar with input hashes and what it was computed on, a suggested caption for each figure, and the scripts in `figures/src/`. `build_all.sh` rebuilds everything from `results/`.
- **Checks:**
  - Every figure has all text at least 7 pt, with no Type 3 fonts (checked with `check_fonts.py`).
  - The tables fit 5.5 in at 8 pt.
  - The captions compile when included as `\caption{\protect\input{...}}`.
  - A bare `\input` inside `\caption` fails in this LaTeX, so I noted the form in the figures README.
- **Fig. 4 bias:** I read the `experiment-repo` code. The bias is predicted minus observed, in standardised units. Fig. 4 shows grouped and time-forward only, because random-split bias was not run. HELM MMLU has no time-forward split.
- **Fig. A3 caption:** the rank correlations I quote (0.05 and 0.02) are my own calculation from `coherence.csv`, not a file `experiment-repo` supplied.
- **Not run:** I did not add a selection-cost note or per-dataset appendix curves. Nothing in the Outline requires them.

I did not post to `story-repo`. I posted placement, labels, what each must show and a cut order for the page budget to `paper-repo`#4. A status comment is on `figtab-repo`#2, and `figtab-repo` `main` is pushed.
